description: SARNO COMMONS is a civic environmental science project developed within ĒGERIA LAB, connected to CNSBII in Italy. We are building an interactive web platform to investigate rainfall trends and environmental changes in the Sarno River basin using NASA Earth observation data. Our goal is to make scientific findings accessible to citizens and educators. We welcome collaborators with skills in Earth science, statistics, satellite data, data visualization and web development.
summary:
SARNO COMMONS is a browser-based civic science project developed within ĒGERIA LAB in connection with CNSBII's environmental observation and education activities. It investigates changes in the Earth system through the Sarno River basin in southern Italy.

The prototype uses NASA GPM IMERG precipitation estimates accessed through NASA POWER to examine rainfall variability from 2001 to 2025. Three initial observation locations, Mercato San Severino, Angri and Scafati, provide interactive charts, annual precipitation totals, linear regression and exploratory Mann–Kendall trend analysis.

The project connects atmospheric data with land cover, waterways, environmental documentation and official geographic sources. Its planned development extends the analysis to the river's sub-basins, rainfall extremes, dry periods and possible relationships with documented environmental events.

SARNO COMMONS distinguishes observations, statistical findings, uncertainty and hypotheses requiring further investigation. It makes NASA Earth observation data accessible to citizens, students and educators while recognizing that satellite precipitation estimates cannot independently establish water pollution or flood risk.
details:
SARNO COMMONS – Investigating Earth System Trends in the Sarno River Basin

Project Overview

SARNO COMMONS is a web-based civic science prototype developed within ĒGERIA LAB, connected to CNSBII's work in environmental education and civic observation.

The project responds to the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" by investigating precipitation variability and potential long-term changes in the Sarno River basin in southern Italy.

It connects three components of the Earth system: atmosphere, land and water.

NASA Data and Scientific Analysis

The prototype uses NASA Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) IMERG precipitation estimates accessed through NASA POWER.

Its initial investigation covers 2001–2025 and examines three observation locations: Mercato San Severino, Angri and Scafati.

Daily precipitation estimates are processed into annual totals and displayed through interactive charts, tables and statistical indicators.

The analytical approach includes ordinary least squares linear regression to estimate the annual rate of change and an exploratory Mann–Kendall test to assess statistical significance.

An initial result for Scafati indicates an estimated trend of approximately +2.8 mm per year, with a Mann–Kendall p-value of 0.4005. The result is not statistically significant at the conventional 0.05 threshold. It therefore does not establish a consistent long-term increase in precipitation.

These preliminary results require further validation, including assessment of serial autocorrelation, satellite uncertainty and the suitability of the selected observation points.

Geographic and Environmental Context

The Sarno River basin is affected by longstanding environmental pressures involving water quality, urban development, wastewater infrastructure and territorial transformation.

SARNO COMMONS combines NASA precipitation information with environmental documentation, official geographic references, the river network and Copernicus land-cover information.

The project also introduces an administrative inventory of 42 municipalities associated with the Sarno environmental Masterplan. These administrative areas are not presented as hydrological catchment boundaries.

The current geographic investigation is exploratory. The three sample locations do not represent the complete river basin.

Planned Scientific Development

The next development stages are designed to extend the investigation to the Solofrana, Cavaiola and other documented contributing sub-basins.

The planned analytical framework includes:

  • Geographic selection using verified watershed boundaries.
  • Spatial aggregation of IMERG precipitation estimates.
  • Rainfall accumulation over 24 hours, 72 hours and seven days.
  • Identification of heavy rainfall episodes and extended dry periods.
  • Long-term precipitation trends and statistical significance testing.
  • Comparison with official hydrological and environmental observations when available.
  • Investigation of possible temporal relationships between rainfall and documented environmental events.

IMERG's approximate 0.1-degree spatial resolution must be considered, particularly for small catchments. The analytical framework will distinguish satellite estimates from ground observations and identify missing or unsuitable data.

These advanced functions remain subject to dataset acquisition, scientific validation and software testing.

Relationship with Water Pollution

Rainfall can influence runoff, river flow and urban drainage. Intense rainfall may affect combined sewer systems, while dry periods can change the relative contribution of treated wastewater to some watercourses.

These relationships justify further investigation but do not establish responsibility for any environmental incident.

NASA precipitation estimates cannot identify chemical contamination, illegal discharges or the operation of wastewater infrastructure.

Reliable environmental assessments require field observations, official infrastructure records, river measurements, water sampling and laboratory analysis.

Civic Science and EGERIA

A future integration with EGERIA, CNSBII's civic environmental reporting system, could support comparisons between precipitation records, documented environmental observations, monitoring stations and verified infrastructure information.

The objective is to identify recurring events and temporal associations that deserve scientific investigation.

The project does not treat statistical correlation as proof of causation.

Technology and Accessibility

SARNO COMMONS uses PHP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

The public website provides responsive navigation, interactive charts, geographical references, scientific explanations and environmental photography.

It works through a standard web browser without requiring registration.

When external data or mapping services are unavailable, the interface communicates the limitation instead of creating fictional scientific measurements.

The project is designed for students, educators, environmental observers and citizens who want to understand Earth observation data.

Innovation and Impact

SARNO COMMONS connects satellite precipitation analysis with a real river basin affected by complex environmental pressures.

Its contribution is to bring together scientific investigation, territorial knowledge and civic participation within an accessible digital environment.

The objective is not simply to display environmental information, but to help users investigate what is changing, where changes may be occurring, whether apparent trends are statistically meaningful and which conclusions require additional evidence.

The Sarno basin serves as the initial case study. With appropriate datasets and validation, the approach could be adapted to other European river basins.

Scientific Integrity and Development Transparency

The project distinguishes measured or estimated data, statistical analysis, hypotheses and planned features.

Original environmental photographs are credited to Michele Buscè and CNSBII.

Generative AI tools assisted with research, writing, coding, debugging, interface design and presentation development. They were not used to fabricate satellite measurements or environmental evidence.

SARNO COMMONS is an independent civic science initiative. NASA has not sponsored or endorsed the project.
